open.notes: Defended: the $1B mark is the priced Series D of May 2022 (TechCrunch, loaded; VCCircle on file). Attack: no later priced round, tender, down round or investor write-down found. Entrackr 2025-10-09 (https://entrackr.com/fintrackr/neobank-unicorn-open-posts-rs-46-cr-revenue-in-fy25-outstanding-losses-mounts-to-rs-1921-cr-10544846) still calls it a unicorn, counts 'over $190 million across rounds' ending with the 2022 IIFL round, and reports FY25 revenue Rs 46 crore, loss Rs 108.8 crore, accumulated losses Rs 1,921 crore; layoffs Apr 2023 (Entrackr headline). Weak business against the mark, but that is not collapse evidence under Rule A, so 1b_plus stands, stale. Entry found: Inc42 2019-02-13 names Speedinvest as a co-lead of the $5M Series A, and lists other firms (Unicorn India Ventures, Recruit) as the existing investors, so this is Speedinvest's first round; TechCrunch and Entrackr of 2019-06-25 then call Speedinvest an existing investor at the Tiger-led Series B. The recorded entry 'undetermined' can become Series A (2019-02), matching the firm card's 'invested 2019'.

entry.quote: Founded in 2015, launched in 2017, and backed by Speedinvest in 2018, Tide has raised more than $200 million to date.

tide.notes: Defended: $1.5B is a priced primary+secondary round (company release 2025-09-22, loaded; TechCrunch 2025-09-21 agrees: '$120 million led by TPG ... at $1.5 billion'); the release lists Speedinvest among funders. Attack: nothing newer found (no 2026 round, sale or IPO; 2026 headlines are operating news, e.g. Luxembourg EU HQ). ENTRY DISPUTES THE RECORD: the recorded entry (Growth, 2019-10, Series B) contradicts the firm's own sentence 'backed by Speedinvest in 2018' (firm post 2025-09-19, on disk) and the firm's archive invest year 2018 (first listed Jan 2019, partner Anthony Danon, who came from Anthemis, a Tide Series A lead). Speedinvest therefore entered in 2018, before the Oct 2019 Series B. The only 2018 round on record is the Aug 2018 GBP 8M bridge (Wikipedia: 'bridge funding from existing investors Anthemis, Creandum and Passion Capital, joined by new investor Augmentum Fintech'), which does not name Speedinvest; a vendor page (not citable) dates Speedinvest's first cheque to a small Dec 2018 Series A extension. No loadable non-vendor source names the 2018 round and ties Speedinvest to it, so round is null; the date 2018 is first-party. The Series B articles loaded (fintech.global, Coverager) name only SBI and Augmentum. The growth post (2025-10-14) lists Tide among '20+ growth investments' of vehicles launched in 2019, which fits a growth-fund follow-on in the Series B, not the entry. Suggest entry_date 2018, stage undetermined (post-Series A, pre-Series B, so not Seed), rather than Growth 2019-10.

entry.quote: in August 2018, we sign a Term Sheet for leading a €2M seed round of a yet to be incorporated company called TIER Mobility

tier.notes: Defended: $2B was a priced round (TechCrunch 2021-10-25, loaded: 'Tier said its micromobility business is now valued at $2 billion', Series D first close, Speedinvest named). Attack succeeds: the Jan 2024 merger with Dott came with only EUR 60M of new equity from existing holders (Mubadala, Sofina and others); SoftBank Vision Fund 2, the Series D co-lead, did not take part (TechCrunch 2024-01-10, loaded); Vision Mobility 2024-01-11 (loaded, citing Manager Magazin) puts the combined company at EUR 150M; Electrive 2024-01-10 cites Handelsblatt on 'a drastically declining company value'. Since then: Oct 2025 EUR 70M Nordic senior secured bond plus a EUR 15M 'Series D extension' at no disclosed price (Zag Daily 2025-10-28, loaded), 2025 first EBITDA-profitable year (headline only). No priced event at $1B+ after 2021, and a documented collapse to about EUR 150M: band should be below_1b, matching Point Nine and Northzone. Legal entity: TIER survives. Tier Mobility SE (Berlin, HRB 236551 B) is active in the register with capital increases in 2025 and 2026 (EUR 4.18M Mar 2025, EUR 4.70M Aug 2025, EUR 5.14M May 2026) and Dott's executives as its managing directors (Maxim Romain replacing Henri Moissinac, Apr 2026) (North Data, loaded: https://www.northdata.com/Tier%20Mobility%20SE,%20Berlin/Amtsgericht%20Charlottenburg%20(Berlin)%20HRB%20236551%20B); Wikipedia gives Dott's formal name as Tier Mobility SE, headquartered in Berlin. So the combined group sits under the TIER entity and only the brand changed to Dott: status private is right, not acquired. Entry: the firm's own Medium post by Mathias Ockenfels (archived copy loaded) says Speedinvest x led the EUR 2M seed, closed Aug 2018, and calls itself 'the very first investor in the company'; TechCrunch 2018-10-23 calls Speedinvest an existing investor at the Northzone-led EUR 25M Series A, which graduates the row. The recorded Seed entry is right; its citation can move from the Series A article to the firm's post.

entry.quote: has raised a $5.5 million round of funding led by Salesforce Ventures, with participation from AngelList, Idinvest, Seedcamp and Speedinvest

wefox.notes: Defended: $4.5B was a priced Series D (TechCrunch 2022-07-11, loaded: '$400 million in a series D round ... post-money valuation of $4.5 billion', Mubadala-led). Attack succeeds on documented collapse: (1) Insurance Journal/Bloomberg 2024-06-14 (loaded): the Series D lead Mubadala backed a sale to Ardonagh at an enterprise value of at most EUR 550M, after a loss of more than EUR 100M and with early holders at risk of losing everything; the board rejected the sale and replaced the CEO. (2) Listed holder Chrysalis Investments wrote the stake down repeatedly: carrying value GBP 126.5M at 2024-03-31 with a warning of a further material cut (QuotedData 2024-07-01, loaded); cut by GBP 35.5M to GBP 56M on an 'uncertainty discount' (QuotedData 2026-01-30, loaded); and at 2026-06-30 'now a 6.2% holding at £39.8m' after a GBP 16.1M waterfall error (https://quoteddata.com/2026/06/chrysalis-uncovers-16m-wefox-blunder-hampering-funds-bid-to-restore-investor-confidence-in-its-valuation/, loaded), which implies roughly GBP 640M (about $0.85B) for the whole company on a straight-line reading, and Chrysalis holds senior terms so the true equity value is lower. (3) The only money since is rescue financing at no stated price: EUR 25M from investors in mid-2024, a EUR 170M refinancing (headline, Jan 2025), EUR 151M in Jul 2025 = EUR 76M equity mainly from existing holders + EUR 75M Searchlight credit (Insurance Journal 2025-07-07, loaded), after selling the Liechtenstein carrier and the Italian units; in 2026 the group still needed EUR 12-15M. No priced round at $1B+ since Jul 2022 (the May 2023 $110M top-up was at the same $4.5B, headline only). Band should be below_1b on collapse evidence; the Seedcamp row ($4.5B) is stale for the same reason and needs aligning. The figure usd is left null: EUR 550M was a rejected offer, not a closed price. Entry: the TechCrunch piece of 2016-01-12 (loaded) names Speedinvest in the $5.5M round led by Salesforce Ventures but does not label the round; TechCrunch 2016-09-20 (loaded) then calls the $28M round the Series A with 'Existing investors Salesforce Ventures, Idinvest, Speedinvest, Seedcamp' on board, so the January round is the pre-Series A (seed) round and the September Series A graduates the row. The 'Seed' label itself comes from sequence, not from the article's words (Seedcamp's own 2016 post calls the $5.5M a Series A, per the Seedcamp book); medium confidence. The recorded entry citation (insurtechdigital) does not name the round either; the TechCrunch pair is the better citation. HQ: press splits; Insurance Journal 2025-07-07 says 'Zurich-based wefox' and the firm card says Switzerland (holding wefox Holding AG, Zurich), while Bloomberg 2024 says 'Berlin-based' and TechCrunch 2022 'German company'. By the rule (where the firm operates) Berlin stands, but the newest company-sourced copy says Zurich: flag for Erik.
